answer: Every identity carves its claim into a shale slab and dyes it with a pigment mixed from its own funding source, then leaves the slab in the gale; a copied pigment washes off while a genuine one bonds into the shale's layers, so only the surviving slab counts as a real claim. The 80 POA pigment-and-carving fee is kept when a slab washes blank, and the identity is barred from carving for five epochs. Ten clones need ten slabs and ten separately mixed pigments; a carver filing a washed slab loses 35 POA of standing per fake, and the cost cannot be pooled or reused.
